To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sequential analysis of message response patterns in computer mediated communication is a useful method to evaluate the effectiveness of computer supported collaborative learning environments, and to predict group interaction patterns.

sequential analysis can be applied to CMC data to identify the way message function, communication style, and discourse rules affect how likely messages are to elicit responses and whether or not a sequence of responses (claim, challenge, explain) mirrors the processes of group decision making, learning, and problem solving.

(a) message response sequences in computer mediated communication are a reflection of group interaction patterns, (b) sequential analysis is an effective tool for measuring group interaction patterns, and (c) the Dialogic Theory provides a theoretical framework and guidelines for using sequential analysis to measure group interaction patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a method for evaluating and modeling group interaction patterns in computer mediated communication (CMC).
the way group interactions are affected by the way people communicate in computer mediated communication environments.
the way people use language to communicate in computer mediated communication (CMC) environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of sequential analysis provides a way to measure and model the way exogenous variables affect message response sequences and group interaction patterns.

the proposed method is a powerful tool for analyzing message response sequences in computer mediated communication and can provide researchers with valuable information about the way group interaction patterns are influenced by the latent and exogenous variables of the system.

sequential analysis can be a valuable tool to measure, model, and predict group interactions in computer-mediated communication and to help researchers understand and improve the effectiveness of group communication in computer mediated environments.
